verdict.rationale: Vercel Sandbox documents running agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs, built to avoid exposing production systems. That implies host-level separation, but the docs never say host secrets or credentials are unreachable, and they describe no credential-handling controls. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that host or platform secrets and credentials are not exposed inside the sandbox, secret-injection or brokering controls, network egress restrictions to stop credential exfiltration, and independent or hands-on verification of the isolation boundary.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can give an agent a sandbox where host secrets and credentials are unreachable by the code it runs

citations.quote: Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs.
Run AI agent output, user uploads, or third-party scripts without exposing your production systems.
Give each AI agent its own Linux user with a private home directory
